vectors.encodes: success false does not mean the payment failed: a pending settlement with a confirmed matching transfer is delivered.
Pending and the chain shows nothing yet: hold. Neither deliver nor refuse.
Receipt found but not deep enough: hold, the 425 case.
The chain could not be read at all: an incomplete check is not a failed payment. Hold, never refuse.
Confirmed, but the transfer went to somebody else than our payTo: refuse.
Confirmed to our payTo but one atomic unit under the quoted price: refuse.
At least the price is enough: a larger transfer is delivered.
Confirmed receipt without any transfer to us: refuse.
Hex addresses compare without regard to letter case: checksum and lower case are the same address.
The reason code decides, the message is free text: a pending code with an unrelated message is still pending.
A different terminal code whose message mentions pending is not pending: refuse.
The same signed payment comes back, the nonce is spent, the transaction is found by nonce and adopted: no second settle, and delivery only on a confirmed matching transfer.
Same retry, but the adopted transaction is not deep enough yet: hold again, still no second settle.
Adopted by nonce while the chain cannot be read: hold, never refuse.
A terminal failure without a broadcast transaction is refused.
A successful settlement is delivered (sanity case outside the pending family).

Pending without the broadcast hash breaks the spec, which says the hash must be present. What a seller does then is not settled: x402 pull request 3437 would treat it as unresolved and not challenge again, while mitaka7210 refuses. Recorded as OPEN, asserted by nobody.
disputed: hold: do not challenge again (x402 pull request 3437, not merged)
refuse: no hash, nothing to reconcile (mitaka7210, kristo-intelligence-6)

vectors.encodes: The named transaction was mined and reverted: the money did not move and that is terminal, unlike pending. Refuse, do not hold. A boolean cannot tell these two apart.
Reverted but only a few blocks deep: a reorganisation could still change the result. Recorded as open, not asserted.

The named hash is a real, confirmed transfer to us for the right amount, but it paid for another payment (other authorization nonce). Recipient and amount alone would deliver; the transfer must also belong to this payment.
Same as the previous case with a larger old transfer and a lower-case recipient: more than the price and the right recipient still do not make it this payment.
The transfer looks right but the authorization nonce cannot be read from the transaction, so it cannot be bound to this payment. Recorded as open, not asserted.
A second wrong-recipient case with another address and a larger amount: the amount does not matter when the money went to someone else.
The quote carries a lower-case address and the chain a checksummed one: still the same recipient, deliver.
Amounts are integers of up to 256 bits. One unit short of a price above 2^53 must be refused; floating point arithmetic reads the two numbers as equal.
The exact price above 2^53 is delivered: refusing large numbers outright is also wrong.

Proof rail (X-Payment-Proof, for buyers whose wallet cannot sign EIP-3009): there is no authorization nonce. The transfer to us, in the quoted token, for enough, from the address that signed the proof, and not delivered before, is delivered. A seller that asks for a nonce here refuses every smart-wallet buyer.

Proof rail: a real, confirmed transfer to us for the right amount, but from another payer than the one who signed the proof, so it paid for another payment. It must not be delivered; refusing or holding are both fine.
Proof rail: everything matches, but this hash was already delivered once. The claim is durable (one hash, one delivery, also after a restart), so it is refused, never delivered a second time.
Authorization rail: the nonce matches and the transfer is right, but this hash was already delivered once. Refused, never delivered a second time.
The transfer goes to us for the right amount but moved another token than the quote asks for. It must not be delivered; refusing or holding are both fine.

The settle response says pending but its transaction is not a hash (not 0x and 64 hex digits). A string that is not a hash is no hash: there is nothing to adopt. Recorded as open because the specification does not say whether to hold or refuse; one deployed seller refuses.
Same family: 0x followed by 64 characters that are not all hex digits is no hash. The seller must not adopt it and keep holding on it; leaving it open or refusing are both fine.
Proof rail: the transaction named in the proof was mined and reverted, so the money did not move. Terminal, refuse.
A token with 18 decimals: one unit short of a price of one whole token. Floating point arithmetic reads the two amounts as equal; refusing or holding are both fine, delivering is wrong.
Proof rail: the transfer looks right but its payer cannot be read, so it cannot be bound to this payment. Recorded as open, not asserted.

Proof rail: the payer differs from the signer of the proof in the last hex digit only. An address is compared whole; a near miss is another payer, so it must not be delivered (refusing or holding are both fine).

Proof rail: the token address differs from the quoted asset in the last hex digit only, and the amount is more than enough. Another token is another token; it must not be delivered (refusing or holding are both fine).
A transaction string that is one byte short (62 hex digits) is no hash. The seller must not adopt it and keep holding on it; leaving it open or refusing are both fine.
